messages:
Maya R: Heads-up — noticed a rare duplicate-kv apply during shard migration in staging this morning. Repro steps below, looking for design/controls to avoid in-prod hits.

Drew W: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro/logs? :thinking:

Maya R: short logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] migration:start shard=33 -> 34 epoch=12
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] prefetch:prefix id=tenant:123/pfx=alpha -> hit
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] apply:kv key=tenant:123:alpha:ctx seq=789 status=ok
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] handoff:commit shard=33 -> 34 completed epoch=12
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] apply:kv key=tenant:123:alpha:ctx seq=789 status=ok <-- duplicate
```
Two identical apply events within ~1s after handoff. Not a client retry (we checked request ids).

Sanjay K: can we confirm the two applies came from different hosts? 

Maya R: yes — host-A (old owner) and host-B (new owner). It looks like both thought they were authoritative for a short window.

Eva L: this smells like the migration handshake didn't strictly quiesce writes. Current handshake is "soft-handoff": old owner forwards writes for 200ms and new owner accepts. We probably need stronger fencing for seq numbers.

Liam P: options: 1) leader epoch fencing (reject apply if epoch < current), 2) per-prefix apply idempotence using a durable seen-map, 3) make handoff blocking (no forwarding) until commit is synced. tradeoffs: 1 is cheap if we already persist epoch; 2 is storage-heavy; 3 increases latency during migration.

Drew W: we do persist migration epoch in the shard manifest but read path doesn't check it on each apply, only on leadership changes. Might just be a path gap during handoff.

Maya R: minimal mitigation: check persisted epoch on apply and reject if apply's source epoch mismatches new owner epoch. That would make old owner fails fast instead of duplicate apply.

Sanjay K: need to be careful with races: if old owner commits locally then tries to forward while new owner already accepted, we must ensure we don't lose the commit. Epoch check will drop old owner's forwarded apply; but if old owner didn't persist it to shared log, data could be lost.

Eva L: right — we need a durable commit protocol: either require old owner to replicate to shared commit log before acknowledging local apply, or ensure forwarded writes always include the write intent and new owner can accept and ack back. Both add complexity.

Liam P: what about making forwarding asynchronous but with a short two-phase handshake: old owner pauses local ack until new owner returns an accept token for that seq. If no response in X ms, fallback to local ack and mark for reconciliation.

Drew W: that adds latency on the hot path for migrations, but migrations are rare and scheduled. For Dedicated customers we can require a strict handoff mode. For hosted, we need a best-effort low-latency mode. So maybe tunable policy: strict vs permissive.

Maya R: proposal: default = permissive with epoch-check on apply + post-handoff reconcile pass (compare commits between owners); strict mode = blocking handoff and epoch fencing. Reconcile pass should detect missing seqs and reapply from durable journal to whichever owner holds primary.

Sanjay K: reconcile pass requires a durable journal of applied seqs. We already have optional replication for some tenants (dedicated). For others we'd need a lightweight commit log: maybe ephemeral WAL on migration that gets shipped on handoff.

Drew W: implementation sketch:
1) During handoff, new owner increments epoch and writes manifest -> persisted.
2) Old owner, before forwarding, reads new epoch; if new epoch > mine, stop local acks and forward all in-flight writes with their local WAL entries.
3) New owner applies writes idempotently using (key, seq, origin-host) tuple and persists applied seq in per-prefix snapshot. If duplicate seq seen, drop.
4) After handoff, run reconcile: compare old owner's WAL tails and new owner's applied seqs; reapply any missing entries from WAL to ensure nothing lost.

Eva L: step 3 requires an idempotency table per prefix. We can make it bounded by rotating checkpoints (GC older seqs once safe). That addresses storage.

Maya R: tests needed: simulate packet reorder, slow persistence on old owner, crash-before-forward. Also add metric alert for "duplicate-apply-count" and "handoff-quiesce-time" so we can detect in prod.

Liam P: +1 on metrics. Also add an invariant check in integration tests: no dup apply within 5s of handoff. Put a canary that migrates heavy prefixes nightly.

Drew W: action items:
- @Drew W to prototype epoch-check-on-apply (non-blocking) and metric for duplicate apply (ETA 3d)
- @Maya R to add repro harness (simulate 2 hosts + handoff races) (ETA 2d)
- @Sanjay K to design reconcile pass and idempotency table GC for review (ETA 1w)

Maya R: I'll also open a postmortem stub in incidents with logs and links. OpsBot: can you create an incident ticket for this? :slightly_smiling_face:

OpsBot: Created incident INC-2026-0342: "staging duplicate-kv-apply during shard migration" assigned to eng-runtime oncall. Link: https://inc.example/INC-2026-0342

Eva L: nits: document policy for strict vs permissive handoff in runbook and console toggle. We'll need SRE signoff for changing defaults.

Maya R: cool. If we land epoch-check quickly we should stop most duplicates and then iterate on reconcile. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
